discussion_comments.comment_body:
Can you also do a test that uses more nested properties? Like:

```
chalk.bold.red.underline`Hello`;
```
Can you add a few more sanity tests for `chalk.stderr`? For example, `chalk.stderr.red.bold('foo')`.
I also couldn't find a test for escaping the arg. Can you add one?
Can you move this out into a helper that accepts `__dirname` as an argument?
Potentially, but this is the only way to really guarantee what we want. I feel more comfortable with this since `supports-color`'s behavior might change.
Does this guarantee that the spawned `node` instance is not supported? I'm failing to see how this is any different than the tests now.
Hm, not sure what you mean. It crashes for me every time. Could you explain?
So recently we had to mock `supports-color` in our tests since CIs handled them differently. Does this test guarantee that no matter what the environment supports, it runs without colors?

Yes, I think so, because it fails everywhere: on CI and on my laptop. It fails when publishing a package with `np`, spawning a process manually in repl, in tests. But if you run `node fixture` directly, it works as expected. I was able to reproduce the crash every time, so I think this failing test is stable.

It will always fail at https://github.com/chalk/supports-color/blob/master/index.js#L44-L46 when running as a spawned instance because `stdout` in [options.stdio](https://nodejs.org/api/child_process.html#child_process_options_stdio) being `pipe` and therefore not being a `TTY`.

It's probably wise to also add a test for the caching of multiple styles, where a new style using the same 'substyle' as the cache is created.

``` javascript
var redBold = chalk.red.bold
var blueBold = chalk.blue.bold
assert.notEqual(blueBold('foo'), redBold('foo')
```

This will catch a more subtle version of the current bug, where the `_styles` array is not shared globally, but per-style. This is what I ran into when attempting a naive fix last night ;-)
